answer: Resist sybils with an atlas of funding links: clustering groups accounts sharing a funder, and each extra identity from one cluster pays a geometrically escalating, non-refundable deposit — a harbor fee that makes mass registration exponentially expensive for an attacker, nearly free for an honest agent. New identities gain influence only after verifiable liveness streaks across epochs, so a flash-built army stays dim like an unlit beacon while genuine agents accrue trust. Limits: funders can be laundered at a cost, and patient botnets can farm liveness — so deposits must burn on fraud.
